super_admin.label: Super-Admin (Platform)
super_admin.blurb: ESAP platform staff. Zero standing access to PHI; cross-tenant reach only through an audited break-glass elevation.

tenant_owner.label: Hospital Admin
tenant_owner.blurb: The hospital contract signatory / CMIO office. Owns roster, units, model display policy and billing.

it_admin.label: IT Admin
it_admin.blurb: Integration lead. Provisions users and wires SSO / SMART / ADT — but never grants clinical roles.

privacy_officer.label: Compliance / Privacy Officer
privacy_officer.scopeLabel: Single tenant, audit and governance only
privacy_officer.blurb: HIPAA Privacy Officer. Lives in the audit log and the fairness panel; cannot open a chart or run a model.

billing_admin.label: Billing Admin
billing_admin.blurb: Revenue-cycle contact. Plan, usage and invoices — no clinical surface at all.

physician.label: Attending Physician
physician.blurb: The primary decision-maker. Runs assessments, reads every Why panel, acknowledges and acts.

resident.label: Resident / Fellow
resident.blurb: Full clinical workspace, but acknowledgements route to an attending for co-sign when the tenant requires it.

np_pa.label: Nurse Practitioner / PA
np_pa.blurb: Independent clinical authority on assigned patients: intake, assess, acknowledge, initiate transfer.

charge_nurse.label: Charge Nurse
charge_nurse.blurb: Owns the unit. Sees every patient risk ranking to allocate staffing and drive the shift handoff.

staff_nurse.label: Staff / Bedside Nurse
staff_nurse.blurb: Captures the intake every model runs on. Reads risk summaries; escalates rather than acknowledges.

case_manager.label: Care Coordinator / Case Manager
case_manager.blurb: Works the discharge-planning view: M-04 readmission and M-05 length-of-stay drive the whole day.

pharmacist.label: Clinical Pharmacist
pharmacist.blurb: Medication-relevant slice only: the drivers that are drug-related, and nothing else.

auditor.label: Quality / QI Auditor
auditor.blurb: Reads the fairness and calibration evidence, exports de-identified cohorts, never exports PHI.

patient.label: Patient / Caregiver
patient.blurb: Sees plain-language, clinician-released content only — never a raw model score.

guest.label: Individual / Guest
guest.blurb: Self-serve tier. The union of patient + self-assessment rights on exactly one seat.

models.name: ICU admission
models.negativeControl: Admission-type ablation drops AUROC to 0.781 — the feature is informative, not leaking.

models.name: 30-day readmission
models.negativeControl: Intake-frame only; discharge-frame features are excluded by construction. Ablation confirms.

models.name: Length of stay

incidents.title: GPU host contention — inference p95 above 900 ms
incidents.detail: The shared GPU also serves the extraction LLM. Tower A inference is queueing behind extraction batches. Mitigation: extraction moved to the overnight window.

incidents.title: ADT feed stalled — no messages for 19 h
incidents.detail: On-prem listener has not received an A01 since 14:10 local. Site VPN tunnel renegotiated at 14:05. Escalated to site IT.

incidents.title: Calibration drift on the Medicaid stratum (M-04)
incidents.detail: Stratified ECE rose from 0.044 to 0.081 over three weeks. M-04 held at 40% traffic; recalibration scheduled.

incidents.title: Tenant suspended for non-payment
incidents.detail: Access disabled; data retained under the 90-day contractual window. No deletion has been performed.

incidents.title: Nightly ETL refresh completed late
incidents.detail: Completed 47 min past the window after a Postgres vacuum. No data gap.

released_results.headline: Your care team reviewed your admission assessment
released_results.plainLanguage: When you came in, the care team used a computer tool that compares your details with many past hospital stays. Dr. Okonkwo has read the result and written the summary below. The tool does not make decisions — your doctor does.
whatThisMeans: The team expects your stay to be a few days rather than a long one.
Your breathing symptoms are the main thing being treated.
You are being watched a little more closely than average because of your heart history.
questionsToAsk: What would need to change for me to go home sooner?
Which of my medicines are for the heart problem, and which are for the breathing?
Who do I call after discharge if the breathlessness comes back?

released_results.headline: Summary from your visit in June
released_results.plainLanguage: This is the plain-language summary your nurse practitioner released after your June visit. It covers what was found and what to watch for.
whatThisMeans: Your blood sugar control was the focus of the visit.
A follow-up blood test was ordered for three months later.
questionsToAsk: Has my follow-up blood test been booked?
Should I change anything about my diet before then?
